# ROM routine map (generated by tests/rom_map.py, step N01; do not edit by hand)

Addresses and counts only; no ROM bytes. Sources: docs/disasm/blocks.txt and docs/disasm/pacman.asm (both stay private), and the coverage of tests/rom_map.cpp.
Definitions: an *entry point* is the reset, NMI, interrupt handler, an RST vector, a call target or an entry of a jump table (RST 20h). A *routine* is the run of instructions from one entry point up to the next one. *Calls* = number of places that call it (CALL, RST, jump-table slot). *Called from* = routines holding such a call. *Tables read* = data blocks (start address) whose address the routine loads.

## Totals
- blocks in blocks.txt: 262 (code 131, other 131)
- code blocks covered exactly once: 131 of 131 (every instruction belongs to exactly one routine)
- instructions in the code blocks: 5439
- entry points / routines: 282
- executed instruction addresses: S27 replay (7,273 frames) 3974, T01a player (60,000 frames) 4533, together 4565 of 5439 (83.9 percent)
- the same as raw machine addresses (prefix steps counted separately): replay 4357, player 4947, together 4987 (the planning measurement for the player was 4,947)
- routines never entered in these runs: 62; routines entered but only partly run: 36
- executed addresses that are not inside any instruction of the map: 0 (prefix bytes DD, FD, ED, CB that the core runs as their own step are counted with their instruction)
- entry points not on an instruction start (ignored): 1 (0066: the NMI vector, which lies in padding data; the board has no NMI)
